chapter.s2.label: Stations
chapter.s2.title: Stations: few and concentrated
fig.stw.title: Six in ten hydrogen stations are in Asia-Pacific
fig.stw.what: Hydrogen stations deployed worldwide at the end of 2024, by region
fig.stw.caption: Source: Interact Analysis, via EV Candi (7 February 2025). It is a single-source count: other counts give different figures, and there is no worldwide count for 2026. EMEA (Europe, Middle East and Africa) is not the same as the EU.
chart.stw.aria: Hydrogen stations at the end of 2024, {n} in total:
chart.stw.five: of all stations are in China, South Korea, Japan, France and Germany
fig.stc.title: Germany went from more than 80 stations to about 50 in two years
fig.stc.what: Stations by country: every bar carries its own date and definition
fig.stc.caption: Dates and definitions differ from country to country, so the bars are not added up and there is no common date axis. Germany: public stations open (13 with 700 bar only, 35 with both pressures, 2 with 350 bar only); for two years earlier the source says “more than 80”, a threshold, not an exact figure. Japan: less than half the 320 the government had planned. California: 11 more stations were temporarily out of service, and average network availability over the last year was close to 60%. China: more than 360 t/day of capacity; an official cited more than 590 stations in June 2026. Sources: electrive.net, Nikkei via Automotive World, California Energy Commission, China Daily.

chapter.s3.label: Price
chapter.s3.title: What a kilo costs
fig.price.title: A kilo of hydrogen costs up to €19 at a German pump
fig.price.what: Price per kilo in Germany (euros) and in China (yuan, not converted), a car's fuel cost per 100 km, and the US goals
fig.price.caption: Germany: gross pump price in January 2026; prices are dynamic and vary by region and pressure (autohaus.de). The truck tariff is net, only with the hylane card and for contracted volumes (solarserver.de). The H2 Mobility cuts come from electrive.net; the sources read give no absolute price before and after. China: China Daily, March 2026. The own calculation uses 0.8 to 0.9 kg per 100 km (new Hyundai Nexo, ecomento.de) at the maximum price. The US Department of Energy figures are goals from its May 2024 plan, not actual costs; its site warns that a new plan is coming.

chapter.s4.label: Trucks
chapter.s4.title: Trucks: series production slips, pilots continue
fig.trucks.title: Series production moved to the 2030s while pilots go on
fig.trucks.what: Milestones from October 2024 to 2030, each with its status
fig.trucks.caption: Done: reported or announced. Pending: awaiting a decision. Plan: an intention, not a delivery. Sources: Daimler Truck (15 September 2026), electrive (several dates), solarserver.de. The postponement of Daimler's series is as recalled by electrive.

chapter.s5.label: Buses
chapter.s5.title: Buses: small fleets
fig.buses.title: US fuel cell bus fleets are small and growing
fig.buses.what: Buses in service and buses approved or planned, by transit agency
fig.buses.caption: Source: FCHEA, the US fuel cell and hydrogen association (an industry source), August 2026. FCHEA itself says operation is concentrated in pilots and relatively small fleets. MTA's 40 is the capacity of its future Gun Hill station; Rochester's 10 are still to be acquired.

chapter.s6.label: Exits and bets
chapter.s6.title: Who leaves and who bets
fig.exits.title: Exits and insolvencies on one side, bets and public money on the other
fig.exits.caption: Sources: CBT News, Automotive Manufacturing Solutions, electrive and gasworld (full list below). Element 2: a winding-up petition was served in September; the article of 3 November 2026 does not confirm the liquidation. The BMW iX5 Hydrogen, the Hilux FCEV and the series production of electrolysers are plans, not facts.

chapter.s7.label: China
chapter.s7.title: China: target and reality
fig.china.title: In the five pilot clusters, 39,023 vehicles sold against a target of 100,000
fig.china.what: Target and sales, two counts of the first half of 2026, stations and the price of a kilo
fig.china.caption: Sources: China Daily (23 March 2026), SMM with data from CAAM (17 July 2026), SNE Research via Asia Business Daily (6 August 2026). CAAM and SNE Research use different definitions (SNE counts commercial vehicles), so the two first-half figures are not compared. In the fourth quarter of 2025 sales exceeded 3,000 units a month. The figures for 2030 are targets.
